name: cadubi
why: Turns rough ASCII sketches into clean box-drawing diagrams, a quirky little transform for the terminal.

brief.what_it_is: CADUBI (Creative ASCII Drawing Utility By Ian) is a full-screen, keyboard-driven text art editor written in Perl that runs in a Unix console. You move a cursor with i, j, k and l, paint characters with a 'pen' that carries a character, foreground and background color, bold, inverse, and blink, and save or load files with Ctrl-o and Ctrl-r. Its output is plain text with console color and attribute codes, meant to be viewed with cat. The README does not say it converts rough sketches into box-drawing diagrams, which is what the scout notes claimed.
brief.why_it_exists: The author wrote it around 1997 to make ASCII art for consoles, which BBSes, email and login prompts use, and the README says it has since become widely packaged on Linux distributions.
brief.how_it_works: CADUBI keeps a 'pen' whose properties (character, colors, bold, inverse, blink) apply to everything you paint or type in text mode. Space paints the pen, and the README says editing works much like common editors such as pico or joe. Output is optimized to take as little space as possible and is intended to display correctly when catted to a terminal.

commands_seen.context: Homebrew install, the first option the README lists.
Debian and Ubuntu install from the distribution packages.
Prints the CADUBI version, copyright and author.
Example that sets a 160x48 workspace, turns off beeping, and opens bacon.txt.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew, Debian and Ubuntu packages need nothing extra. Building from source needs Perl 5.002 or later and the Term::ReadKey Perl module. No accounts or hardware are mentioned. Use -s or --size if the console is not the default size, and make sure the console really is that size or the text will not wrap correctly.
brief.standout: It is a 1990s Perl console tool that is still packaged everywhere, and its editing model is built around a persistent pen with text mode and color/attribute toggles, not around producing diagrams. The author's own framing is that the code has barely changed since it was written.
brief.status: quiet. The README gives no version number, release date, or recent commit information. It says the code 'hasn't changed much since' about 1997, but it also says the package is still available on most Linux distributions. Last-commit date was not checked.
brief.caveats: The scout notes describe a box-drawing transform, and the README says nothing like that, so the entry should describe it as an interactive editor. Requires a Unix-style console. Source builds need Perl and Term::ReadKey. The README says blink is 'regarded as highly annoying' and is off by default. Reading a file loads only what fits in the workspace. The -s size setting only works if the real console matches it. Licensing was not stated in the README text fetched.
quotes: This Perl program was written sometime around 1997 -- many years before I knew anything about Perl or Unix -- and the code hasn't changed much since then.
CADUBI is an application written in Perl that allows you to draw text-based images that are viewable on typical unix-based consoles.
You'll notice that editing is much like common text editors, such as pico or joe.
